definitions.explanation: The wavering visual distortion caused by heated air rising from the ground on hot days.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{道|みち}に{陽炎|かげろう}が{立|た}つ。
examples.english: Heat shimmer rises from the summer road.

examples.japanese: {陽炎|かげろう}で{遠|とお}くの{景色|けしき}が{揺|ゆ}れて{見|み}える。
examples.english: The distant scenery appears to waver due to the heat haze.

examples.japanese: {真夏|まなつ}の{昼下|ひるさ}がり、アスファルトの{上|うえ}に{陽炎|かげろう}が{揺|ゆ}らめいていた。
examples.english: In the midsummer afternoon, heat haze was shimmering above the asphalt.

notes:
SEASONAL REFERENCE:
{陽炎|かげろう} is a traditional spring seasonal word ({季語|きご}) in haiku, though it is most commonly observed on hot summer days.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {陽炎|かげろう}が{立|た}つ (heat haze rises)
- {陽炎|かげろう}が{揺|ゆ}らめく (heat haze shimmers)

The phenomenon creates a dreamlike, ephemeral quality often used as a literary metaphor for things that are fleeting or illusory.
